text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 3.4% today after oil prices rose sharply, with U.S. crude climbing to nearly $100 a barrel and world oil prices hitting $107—the stock's biggest single-day gain in over a week. The move reverses earlier losses; the company had fallen 8.6% over the past two weeks as markets worried about potential Iran peace deals that could flood global oil supplies. Today's rally reflects shifting sentiment: despite Trump administration officials saying de-escalation is possible, Secretary of State Rubio signaled negotiations remain stuck on Iranian demands, keeping geopolitical risk premiums in the market and supporting oil prices that fuel refiner profits.

Refineries are running at 94.5% capacity and storage levels remain moderate, so the refining sector benefits directly when crude prices hold firm—there's no glut of inventory forcing margins down. The broader dynamic here is uncertainty: every headline hint of peace talks sends oil lower (as happened last Monday), while diplomatic setbacks prop it back up, creating the kind of volatility that has whipsawed the stock.
